title: Calls between compiled functions
summary: Proves a call statement from the callee's Implements theorem: the results represent the callee's value as owned, every array the caller borrowed or owned is kept, and the memory's maximum size is unchanged, so a second call has room.  For a callee that returns a word and keeps the store, KeepsEntry also keeps the trees the caller holds.
premises: An Implements theorem for the callee at its entry index
The entry is a defined function, not an import, with as many parameters as the call has arguments
The arguments evaluate to words that represent the callee's input as borrowed
The allocator invariant, Separate for the blocks the callee consumes, and a memory cap of at most 65,535 pages
The result locals can hold any value that represents the callee's result
result: The call leaves in the result locals values that represent the callee's result as owned, with the allocator invariant, every earlier borrowed or owned array apart from the consumed blocks kept and apart from the result, and the memory's maximum size unchanged.
